relevance_note: Case series of three patients, two with Blau syndrome and NOD2 variants described individually: 'genetically diagnosed with Blau syndrome with CARD15/NOD2 mutation (N670K)' (Case 1) and '(C495Y)' (Case 2).
method_note: Hand-built from a careful reading; a short Python script in the scratch directory only assembled the JSON and checked spans. Case 3 has cryopyrin-associated periodic syndrome with an NLRP3 variant (Y859C), no NOD2 variant and no Blau diagnosis, so is out of scope (no rows); counted in cohort_size_as_stated = 3. is_proband left null: the paper presents three unrelated patients and never uses 'proband' or 'index case'. Age at diagnosis records the first (clinical, biopsy-based) diagnosis; genetic diagnosis was at 13 years (Case 1) and 5 years (Case 2), quoted in clinical_diagnosis_basis. Ethnicity 'Japanese' from the statement naming the three consecutive patients. Vital status 'alive' from the present-tense current-status descriptions. Variants printed as protein-style short forms (N670K, C495Y) without 'p.' or transcript; recorded unchanged in variant_original_string and protein_hgvs_as_stated; no cDNA printed. Pathogenicity not stated beyond 'mutation'. Several features are reported absent at one time and present at another (Case 1: no arthropathy at 5 months, arthropathy at 2 years; no uveitis at 2 years, uveitis from 10 years; Case 2: no intraocular inflammation at 1.5 and 21 years; normal optic discs at 21 years after earlier swelling). These are time-specific, not contradictions; excluded rows carry the time in severity_or_detail and the checklist uses the observed state. Case 2 visual impairment checklist left 'not reported': good visual acuity maintained but slightly reduced acuity in the left eye from aftercataract. Case 2 uveitis left 'not reported': optic disc swelling described as an isolated ocular manifestation with no intraocular inflammation, and the word uveitis is not applied to him. Case 1 elevated inflammatory markers marked observed from 'C-reactive protein returned to the normal level' (implies prior elevation); CRP 5.8 mg/dL and ESR 48 mm/1 h at 2 years are printed without being called elevated. Retinal periphlebitis/capillaritis (Case 1) is retinal vasculitis, not the large-vessel or leukocytoclastic vasculitis of the checklist, so vasculitis is 'not reported'. Sausage-like finger swelling is not recorded as tenosynovitis. Inconsistencies in the paper: Case 1's skin diagnosis is at 5 months in the case report and abstract but 'at the age of 6 months' in the Discussion; Case 2's optic disc swelling began 'At 8 years old' in the abstract and 'At the age of 8.5 years' in the case report. The paper writes 'afferent pupillary detect' (typo for defect); quoted as printed. The group sentence 'The two patients with Blau syndrome showed skin rashes, remittent fever, and arthralgia' was recorded as a named-group positive statement for both.
